claim.why_it_matters: 15.73.3 rule 1 gives the normative arithmetic expression that native-arithmetic FUNCTION PI approximates. The PDF prints the fractional part as one unbroken 31-digit run; the markdown injects a space before the final two digits ('...327 95'). No digit is lost or altered, but any reader or tool copying the constant can truncate at the space and silently obtain 0.14159265358979323846264338327 - wrong from the 30th decimal onward.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent pixel measurement, not by re-reading OCR. Rendered specs page 933 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v933/spec_p933.png, 2550x3300) and ran a column-ink profile over the two constant lines.

RULE 1 line (y 1380-1430): the only interior blank gaps >= 10 px are at x=590 (17 px) and x=626 (15 px) - those are the two real spaces flanking the '+' in '(3 + 0.'. Every gap inside the digit run after '0.' measures 3-7 px, i.e. ordinary inter-glyph kerning. There is NO space anywhere in the fractional digits. Connected-ink-run count for the line = 37, exactly '(' + '3' + '+' + '0' + '.' + 31 digits + ')'. So the PDF prints an unbroken 31-digit run, and the claim quotes the PDF correctly.

MARKDOWN: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 37348 is literally '(3 + 0.14159265358979323846264338327 95)'. Codepoint dump shows U+0020 at index 36, i.e. inside the numeric literal, after the 29th fractional digit. The claim quotes the markdown correctly. This is a genuine injected character, not reflow, not a line wrap, not page-break furniture: the space sits mid-token on a single short line that is nowhere near the measure, so no wrapping mechanism can explain it.

CONTENT IMPACT: deleting the space restores '1415926535897932384626433832795' = pi - 3 to 31 decimal places, matching the PDF digit-for-digit. No digit is lost or altered, so the corruption is confined to tokenization - but the failure mode the claim names is real: truncation at the space yields 0.14159265358979323846264338327, which diverges from pi at the 30th decimal. Ruled out the benign explanations and the claim still stands.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS INCOMPLETE: the identical defect occurs a second time on this same page, in 15.73.3 rule 3, and the claim does not mention it. Line 37356 reads '3.14159265358979323846264338327 9503.' with U+0020 at index 31. Pixel profile of the rule-3 line (y 1850-1900) shows a maximum interior gap of 8 px - no space at all - and 36 ink runs = '3' + '.' + 33 digits + '.', so the PDF prints an unbroken 3.141592653589793238462643383279503. That instance is the more consequential of the two: rule 3 states the standard-decimal returned value is 'exactly' this number, so it is a normative exact constant rather than an implementor-defined approximation, and truncation at the injected space would produce a value wrong from the 30th decimal in a rule that admits no tolerance.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, but under-scoped and under-rated. Two spurious U+0020 characters are injected inside numeric literals on page 933 (15.73 PI function, 15.73.3 Returned value rules), not one:

  1. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:37348 (rule 1, native arithmetic - implementor-defined approximation)
     markdown: (3 + 0.14159265358979323846264338327 95)
     PDF:      (3 + 0.1415926535897932384626433832795)

  2. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:37356 (rule 3, standard-decimal arithmetic - the value the rule calls 'exactly')
     markdown: 3.14159265358979323846264338327 9503.
     PDF:      3.141592653589793238462643383279503.

In both cases the space falls after the 29th fractional digit. Verified by 300 dpi column-ink profiling: no interior gap on either line exceeds 8 px within the digit run (real spaces on this page measure 15-17 px), and ink-run counts confirm 31 and 33 fractional digits respectively, matching the markdown's digit content exactly. No digit is lost or altered in either literal, so this is a transcription/tokenization defect rather than a value error.

Fix: delete both U+0020 characters. Severity should be raised from 'cosmetic' to 'minor' on account of instance 2 - a reader or extraction tool that splits on whitespace silently obtains 3.14159265358979323846264338327 for a constant the standard declares exact, an error at the 30th decimal in a normative exact value.
